## Why

Model-visible settings diffing was split between the typed environment world state and ad hoc builders in `context_manager/updates.rs`. That left the in-memory world baseline incomplete, duplicated initial-context rendering, and meant environment changes during a multi-iteration turn could reach the next sampling request with stale context.

This PR is stacked on #29249.

## What changed

- Add separate typed `WorldState` sections for model, permissions, collaboration mode, multi-agent mode, realtime state, and personality; each section owns only its topic comparison and fragment rendering.
- Pass each section an optional previous value, distinguishing an absent section from a persisted optional value without sentinel defaults or nested options.
- Return ordered `ContextualUserFragment`s from world-state rendering and let the context consumer merge adjacent same-role fragments into messages.
- Build initial world context through `WorldState::render_full()`, including render-only environment subagent data and personality gating; retain model-switch and realtime-shutdown as transition-only overlays.
- Store the latest in-memory `WorldState` snapshot on `ContextManager` next to the durable `TurnContextItem` reference.
- Rebuild world state from the live environment snapshot before each sampling iteration and inject only its rendered diff.
- Seed or refresh the world baseline during resume reconstruction, compaction, and context-window replacement.
- Preserve the legacy single-environment rendering while allowing initial fragment ordering and message grouping to follow world-state assembly.

## Context

This is PR 1 of a five-PR prerequisite stack for [CCA-50](https://linear.app/openai/issue/CCA-50/support-environment-scoped-mcp-file-transfer-in-cca) and the [CCA file-transfer RFC](https://app.notion.com/p/3878e50b62b0817c9abfc359cf1d5979).

The previous whole-file relay approach in #28337 can exceed the 64 MiB Noise message limit and puts file bytes on the CCA control plane. The replacement architecture keeps file bytes inside the selected executor. Its first prerequisite is a bounded filesystem read that works identically through both direct and sandbox-helper paths.

Stack order:

1. bounded executor reads (this PR)
2. versioned prepared-upload protocol
3. prepared snapshot lifecycle
4. protected HTTPS upload execution
5. spawned-server transport and reconnect E2E

## What changed

- Add optional `maxBytes` to `fs/readFile` without changing legacy callers.
- Enforce the limit before returning oversized contents from direct reads.
- Forward and enforce the same limit through the sandbox helper.
- Return a stable protocol error without relaying oversized bytes.

This PR does not add file-transfer RPCs or enable any new CCA behavior.

- `cargo check -p codex-exec-server` (passed during exact-stack validation)

## Context

This is PR 4 of the five-PR prerequisite stack for [CCA-50](https://linear.app/openai/issue/CCA-50/support-environment-scoped-mcp-file-transfer-in-cca) and the [CCA file-transfer RFC](https://app.notion.com/p/3878e50b62b0817c9abfc359cf1d5979). It is stacked on #29444.

The old relay approach in #28337 sends whole file bodies through the CCA/Noise control plane and can exceed the 64 MiB message limit. This PR adds the executor-owned data plane: only bounded metadata and operation IDs traverse RPC; prepared bytes stream directly from executor memory to a broker-issued destination.

## What changed

- Advertise `preparedFileUpload` only when an explicit development gate is enabled; release builds are hard-disabled even if the environment variable is present.
- Add `startUpload` with a two-stage state/quota recheck around asynchronous descriptor validation.
- Stream 64 KiB chunks from zeroizing prepared storage without cloning the whole file.
- Restrict descriptors to bounded HTTPS PUT URLs on trusted suffixes, port 443, a minimal header allowlist, and 30-second to 10-minute expiry.
- Resolve with a timeout, reject reserved/private addresses, pin validated addresses, disable proxies, and disable redirects.
- Limit each session to two active uploads.
- Report `completionUnknown` after dispatch when cancellation, timeout, transport loss, or a non-success response makes remote completion ambiguous.
- Preserve status reconciliation across a resumed transport session.

Localhost HTTP is accepted only in debug builds for hermetic E2E. This remains an executor prerequisite: there is no Codex Core consumer or production CCA enablement in this PR.

## Summary

- add the read-only v2 `marketplace/checkUpdates` RPC
- check every configured Git marketplace, or one exact marketplace by name
- share remote-revision resolution and the installed-snapshot predicate with `marketplace/upgrade`

## Contract

`marketplaceName` is optional. When omitted, the response contains every configured Git marketplace in stable name order.

```json
{
  "marketplaceName": "team-tools"
}
```

```json
{
  "results": [
    { "status": "upToDate", "marketplaceName": "current" },
    { "status": "updateAvailable", "marketplaceName": "changed" },
    {
      "status": "error",
      "marketplaceName": "private-tools",
      "message": "failed to resolve remote revision: ..."
    }
  ]
}
```

Each marketplace produces one result:

- `upToDate`: the remote revision matches `lastRevision`, the installed manifest exists, and install metadata matches the configured source, ref, sparse paths, and revision.
- `updateAvailable`: the remote resolves, but an upgrade would do work. This includes a new revision, a missing snapshot, or damaged/mismatched install metadata.
- `error`: the remote revision cannot be resolved. Errors are isolated per marketplace so other results are still returned.

An exact name that is unknown or refers to a local marketplace is an invalid request. The check does not write config, replace installed snapshots, or invalidate plugin caches.

This is a separate RPC instead of a `dryRun` field on `marketplace/upgrade` so compatibility fails closed: an older server returns method-not-found rather than ignoring an unknown field and performing an upgrade.

## Validation

- `just test -p codex-app-server-protocol` — 248 passed
- `just test -p codex-core-plugins` — 264 passed
- `just test -p codex-app-server marketplace_check_updates` — 3 passed

- scoped `just fix` for `codex-core-plugins`, `codex-app-server-protocol`, and `codex-app-server`

## Summary

Resolves #26234.

Codex uses the OpenAI Responses API `type: "namespace"` wrapper to serialize namespaced tools. Support for that wire format is not universal among third-party Responses-compatible endpoints: some reject it, while others may not preserve its namespace semantics. On endpoints that only support plain function tools, this can prevent MCP tools, deferred `tool_search` results, and standalone extension tools from being exposed or called correctly.

This change adds a Codex-side compatibility fallback rather than requiring those endpoints to implement namespace wrappers. Codex keeps its logical namespaced tool model internally, but serializes model-visible tools based on the provider's `namespace_tools` configuration/default: preserve namespace wrappers when enabled, or emit canonical flattened function names when disabled. Flat calls are resolved back to the original namespaced runtime, preserving logical tool identity.

## What Changed

- Added optional `namespace_tools` provider capability/config plumbing. Explicit config wins; OpenAI-auth and Azure Responses providers preserve wrappers by default; configured non-OpenAI Responses providers flatten by default; Amazon Bedrock keeps wrappers by default but can opt out with `namespace_tools = false`.
- Centralized model-visible namespace serialization: preserve `type: "namespace"` when supported, otherwise emit canonical `<namespace>__<tool>` function names for direct tools and deferred `tool_search` results.
- Kept flat calls executable by registering flat aliases back to namespaced runtimes while preserving logical tool identity.
- Kept generic `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` hook matching compatible with model-visible flat names via matcher-only aliases, while preserving the existing canonical hook name in hook stdin.
- Kept tool discovery and standalone extension tools available independently from namespace wrapper support, including flattened deferred MCP specs and Responses Lite `web.run` / `image_gen.imagegen`.
- Validated canonical flat names before exposure: app-server rejects duplicate or overlong flattened dynamic-tool names, MCP normalization disambiguates canonical-flat collisions, and core fails fast only when a collision can reach the model or `tool_search`. Hidden/unreachable-only collisions keep their logical runtimes while warning and suppressing the ambiguous flat alias.
- Propagated `namespace_tools` through remote thread config and regenerated the config schema.
- Added regression coverage for provider defaults/Bedrock opt-out, app-server dynamic validation, MCP normalization, flat registry dispatch, reachable/discoverable collision fail-fast, hidden-only alias suppression, deferred MCP discovery, Responses Lite standalone tools, and flattened hook aliases.

Add `features.concurrent_reasoning_summaries` as the kill switch.

With it on, normal turns send `stream_options.reasoning_summary_delivery=concurrent_cutoff`. Codex ignores partial summary events and only renders `reasoning_summary_text.done` for the current reasoning item, dropping late completions. It buffers completed items by `output_index` so history and lifecycle events stay in response order, and keeps an active custom-tool diff stream alive when an older reasoning item completes.

Example rollout from ResponsesAPI:

```text
reasoning 0 added
summary 0 done              # rendered
summary 1 done              # rendered
summary 2 starts
message 1 added
message 1 text streams
summary 2 done              # dropped; reasoning 0 is no longer current
reasoning 0 done
message 1 completed
```

ResponsesAPI can keep summary work running after the message starts. Codex keeps the completed summaries that arrived while reasoning 0 was current, drops the late one, and preserves response order if later `output_item.done` events arrive before earlier ones.

This is intentionally narrower than the general interleaved-item approach: it does not make partial summary deltas item-addressable or change TUI replay. With the flag off, `stream_options` is omitted and existing summary behavior is unchanged.

Validated with the focused concurrent-summary, output-order, apply-patch streaming, and WebSocket prewarm tests, plus `cargo build -p codex-cli --bin codex`.

## Summary
- Reason: Codex Apps needs a debugger endpoint that can inspect the current session's runtime `tool_search` behavior without approximating BM25 or reading only raw MCP/plugin inventories.
- Intention: Expose metadata-only debug results from the same effective runtime tool router and `ToolSearchHandler` path used by live `tool_search`, while preserving production ranking and exposure behavior.
- Scope: Adds one experimental app-server v2 RPC, protocol types/schema output, and focused core diagnostics/tests. This does not implement the paused ranking semantic changes or change normal model-visible tool search behavior.
- Outcome: App clients can call `debug/toolSearch/search` with `threadId`, `query`, and optional `limit` to receive the exact coalesced tool payload plus debug metadata such as indexed/matching counts, truncation, source/search text, rank, and finite BM25 score.

This is the narrow backend API for the tool search debugger: one app-server method backed by the runtime `tool_search` path, with debug fields kept out of production tool execution.

## Technical Details
- Approach: `ToolSearchHandler::search_with_debug` uses one bounded BM25 search as the authoritative source for ranked entries and the coalesced tools payload, plus an unbounded search only for match-count and truncation metadata. The request is routed through `ToolRouter`, `ToolRegistry`, `Session`, and `CodexThread`.
- Code pointers:
  - `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/tool_search.rs`: builds internally consistent debug metadata and current coalesced `tool_search` output.
  - `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/tool_search_processor.rs`: validates request params, loads the thread, invokes runtime search, and serializes metadata-only JSON payloads.
  - `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/tool_search.rs`: defines `ToolSearchSearchParams`, `ToolSearchSearchResponse`, and `ToolSearchSearchResult`.
  - `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs`: registers experimental `debug/toolSearch/search`.
- Notes: Because `debug/toolSearch/search` is experimental, stable generated TS does not include the full client request wrapper unless the consumer uses experimental app-server codegen. The wire params are `threadId`, `query`, and nullable optional `limit`; response fields are camelCase.

## Stack

1. [#30956](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/30956) — isolate legacy item fanout
2. [#30283](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/30283) — emit canonical `TurnItem` lifecycle ← **this PR**
3. [#30188](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/30188) — persist canonical items for paginated threads

## Description

This PR makes canonical `TurnItem` lifecycle the live source of truth for these items:
- command execution
- dynamic tool calls
- collab agent tool calls
- sub-agent activity

These are new TurnItems added in https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/30282, which only previously had the legacy-style `EventMsg::*Begin/End` events. This PR switches core to emit these as `ItemStarted` / `ItemCompleted` + `TurnItem` instead, and app-server v2 handles those canonical item events directly.

Core still fans canonical item events back out into the old legacy `EventMsg` forms where we still need them for legacy rollout persistence, rollout trace, and raw core event consumers. App-server ignores that compatibility fanout so v2 clients do not get duplicate item notifications.

Rollout persistence behavior is unchanged in this PR.

Legacy conversion code lives in `protocol/src/legacy_events.rs` from #30956; this PR adds the projections for the migrated item families there.

## Why

This is the second PR in the stack for making ThreadHistoryBuilder stateless, which relies on using `TurnItem`. First PR is at: https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/30282

## Follow-up

The next PR https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/30188 actually writes `TurnItem` to rollout files when using `thread.history_mode = "paginated"`.

## Why

Codex users need a temporary way to send referral invites from `/usage` without adding a public app-server API. Reward eligibility and terms are backend-owned and conditional, so the client must not promise that sending an invite grants a usage reset.

## What changed

- add a temporary client-owned referral invite flow under `/usage`
- call the existing ChatGPT referral HTTP endpoints directly instead of adding app-server RPC/protocol endpoints
- reuse the embedded app-server auth session, pin user/workspace identity and the server-provided offer, and hide the flow when a referral client is unavailable
- require email entry plus explicit confirmation, revalidate the offer immediately before send, and send the invite with a no-retry/no-redirect POST client
- display the backend-provided offer description, with neutral `Invite a friend to Codex` fallback copy when no description is returned

## Scope

- 24 files, 1,177 additions, 26 deletions
- no new backend endpoint or public app-server API

## TUI preview

```text
/usage

  Usage
  View account usage or redeem an earned reset.

  1. Show usage                View recent account token usage.
  2. Redeem usage limit reset  Check reset availability.
  3. Invite someone to Codex   Invite a friend to Codex.

EMAIL

  Invite someone to Codex
  Enter one email address, then press Enter.

  name@example.com

CONFIRMATION

  Send referral invite?
  Invite a friend to Codex.
  Recipient: friend@example.com
  • Your friend must be new to Codex.
  By sending, you confirm that you have this person's consent.

  1. Send invite
  2. Cancel                    (selected by default)

SENDING

  Invite someone to Codex
  Sending an invite to friend@example.com...

SUCCESS

  Invite someone to Codex
  Invite sent to friend@example.com.
```

## HTTP request shape

```http
GET /backend-api/referrals/invite/eligibility?referral_key=codex_referral_persistent_invite&requested_referrals=1&supports_rewardless_invites=false
GET /backend-api/wham/referrals/eligibility_rules?referral_key=codex_referral_persistent_invite

POST /backend-api/wham/referrals/invite
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "referral_key": "codex_referral_persistent_invite",
  "emails": ["friend@example.com"]
}
```

The client re-fetches the offer and verifies the user, workspace, and current server-provided offer and rules before making the single-attempt POST. The invite result separately reports whether a reward was included; the UI does not promise a specific reward.

## Testing

- `just test -p codex-tui referrals` (7 passed)

## Summary

Direct Codex third-party traffic receives safety-buffering metadata from the Responses WebSocket without Codex first-party treatment headers. This change reads the new optional `safety_buffering.retry_model` wire field, forwards it through the existing internal/app-server `fasterModel` notification, and leaves the explicit user retry flow unchanged.

API review: https://app.notion.com/p/38c8e50b62b081308e4ae4719443db6b

Paired Responses API producer: https://github.com/openai/openai/pull/1082770

## Behavior

- With no first-party treatment metadata, an object-valued safety-buffering signal is visible and uses the wire `retry_model` value.
- On repeated buffering updates in one response, an omitted field preserves the prior retry target and explicit `null` clears it.
- First-party treatment headers remain authoritative for both visibility and retry target, including explicit disabled and enabled-without-target treatments.
- Treatment and cached wire state reset for every `response.create`, even when the WebSocket connection is reused.
- Missing and explicit `null` on the first object remain compatible and produce no retry target.
- SSE behavior is unchanged: its existing first-party treatment headers remain authoritative, and Responses does not emit this public field on SSE.

The retry remains explicit and user initiated. It creates an ordinary request with the selected model; all ordinary access, safety, and rate-limit checks still apply.

## Validation

- `just test -p codex-api`: 136 passed, including direct WebSocket string, missing, null, repeated omission, explicit-null clearing, and 1P treatment precedence.
- `just test -p codex-app-server --test all direct_websocket_safety_buffering_reaches_app_server_notification`: passed. This uses a mock WebSocket server and proves `retry_model` reaches the real `model/safetyBuffering/updated` notification as `fasterModel` without leaking a disabled warmup treatment across responses on the same connection.
- `just test -p codex-tui safety_buffering_offers_one_retry_with_app_wording`: passed and proves the exact model becomes the existing `RetrySafetyBufferedTurn` action.
- `just fix -p codex-api`, `just fix -p codex-app-server`, and `just fmt`: passed.
- Paired Responses producer validation exercised the real WebSocket route/emitter under mocked auth, Statsig, and Protection Client boundaries for configured string, explicit null, and disabled/omitted cases; the unshipped draft wire name `faster_model` was absent.

## Why

`currentTime/read` has a fixed total request budget, but the wait to enqueue its outbound request on the shared channel was outside that budget. Under backpressure, the app server could dispatch the request after the caller's deadline, leading to late work and misleading timeout behavior. Increasing the timeout would only mask the queue contention.

This change makes the deadline behavior deterministic while we continue investigating the broader queue and instrumentation design. The structured timing work in [#30334](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/30334) remains the foundation for that follow-up.

## What changed

- Added a deadline-aware single-connection outbound request path that bounds both queue admission and response wait.
- `currentTime/read` now uses that path, so its 10-second budget covers the outbound queue.
- Applied the same safety property to attestation generation requests, which use the same client-request pattern.
- Ensured a request that times out before queue admission does not leave a pending callback behind.
- Added a regression test for a full outbound queue.

## Testing

- `just test -p codex-app-server deadline_expires_while_waiting_for_outgoing_queue_capacity`
- `just fix -p codex-app-server`

The broader app-server suite was also attempted, but unrelated sandbox-dependent tests cannot run in this environment because macOS Seatbelt operations fail with `sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted`.

## Why

Malformed client-executed `tool_search_call.arguments` can be returned by the Responses service and persisted verbatim. Once written to a rollout, the malformed call is replayed on every follow-up and cold resume, leaving the session permanently unusable. This prevents future occurrences of [#26379](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/26379); already-poisoned rollouts remain out of scope.

## What Changed

- Keep `rawResponseItem/completed` faithful to the original server item while canonicalizing client tool-search calls before durable history and rollout persistence.
- Re-serialize valid arguments through `SearchToolCallParams`, replace malformed arguments with a bounded placeholder, and keep missing or empty call IDs out of durable history.
- Produce a matching empty `tool_search_output` for malformed calls with usable IDs, and keep parse diagnostics payload-free.
- Leave server-executed tool-search calls unchanged.
- Add an end-to-end regression test covering malformed arguments, unknown fields, missing and empty call IDs, server execution, raw event fidelity, follow-up pairing, rollout contents, and cold resume.

## Verification

`just test -p codex-core --retries 0 malformed_tool_search_is_repaired_before_persistence_and_resume` passes and exercises an oversized multilingual argument key through persistence and cold resume.

## Why

When Codex exits in response to an enhanced keyboard event, the terminal can deliver the corresponding key-release event after shutdown has started. We reset keyboard reporting before returning to the parent shell, but bytes that were already encoded as CSI-u input can remain queued in stdin, leaving shells to display fragments such as `9;1:3u` as literal input.

This is a common experience for me -- here's a simple example:


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9aa51710-84c3-4de9-8cfc-c2bc4083b2ef

## What changed

After restoring terminal modes and finishing stderr handling in `restore_after_exit`, reuse the existing platform-specific input-buffer flush. This discards events queued under Codex keyboard reporting before the parent shell resumes, while leaving the ordinary temporary-restore path and external APIs unchanged.

Closes https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/24026.
items.title: Flush queued terminal input before exit

items.body:
## Why

When `codex` starts, terminal probing and potentially slow configuration, cloud, model, and MCP work happen before the normal TUI event stream owns stdin. Text typed immediately can remain in the tty queue or straddle reader and decoder handoffs, so only part of the prompt appears once the first frame renders.

This is the startup-side inverse of #31192. We want it to be safe to begin typing as soon as the command starts, without letting an early Enter or control key confirm a startup screen, submit an invisible draft, or escape into the parent shell when startup fails.

## What changed

- claim stdin in `PreparedTerminal::prepare()` before slower startup work, using a bounded capture mode that keeps terminal signals and output post-processing active
- preserve text, backspaces, multiline bracketed paste, UTF-8, CSI, and SS3 boundaries while transferring input through terminal probing, startup screens, the OSS picker, activation, and the persistent crossterm reader
- restore captured text only to the composer and quarantine submission or action keys until stdin is drained, the composer has rendered once, and the initial quiet boundary has elapsed, including custom submit bindings
- restore terminal state and flush captured input on failed, cancelled, or exiting startup paths, and prevent the local model downloader from inheriting stdin

## Safety

Startup does not enter full raw mode: Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Z remain live, and ordinary newline output keeps its normal processing. Confirmation screens get their own protected draw boundary, inline mode re-anchors after startup output, partial terminal sequences remain under one decoder owner, and every capture buffer has a hard bound.

Unix PTY coverage exercises early capture, activation, signals, output processing, partial input, restoration, and flushing. Focused parser, event-stream, startup-screen, composer, and OSS-picker coverage passes, as do scoped Clippy and formatting. The full TUI run passed 3,091 tests; its four failures were two existing Guardian expectations plus a plugin refresh test and a timing-sensitive startup-probe test that pass in isolation. Windows parser and event-coalescing behavior is covered, but an end-to-end Windows console lifecycle test remains follow-up work.

## Review note

This is intentionally a draft because the safety invariant crosses terminal ownership, decoding, startup-screen routing, and the final event-stream handoff. The diff is correspondingly large. A size review recommended staging the independent exit flush in #31192, a behavior-neutral Unix probe extraction, the persistent event-broker infrastructure, and then the user-visible early-capture behavior. I kept the final behavior atomic here because splitting it by platform or startup phase would recreate the lost-input and hidden-confirmation gaps; I can restack the prerequisite pieces after the architecture is agreed.

## What

## Background
- OpenAI file uploads currently collapse reqwest send failures into one generic message, making it difficult to tell whether a failure was a timeout, connection issue, or streamed-body failure.

## Changes
- Add a low-cardinality reqwest error class to the existing `OpenAiFileError::Request` message: `timeout`, `connect`, `body`, `request`, or `unknown`.
- Populate the same class at the existing create, blob upload, and finalize request boundaries without changing request construction, timeouts, retries, or upload behavior.

## Follow Ups
- None.

- `just fmt`
